definitions.explanation: A small stick with cotton wrapped around one or both ends, used for cleaning ears, applying medicine or cosmetics, and other purposes.

examples.japanese: {綿棒|めんぼう}で{耳|みみ}を{掃除|そうじ}する。
examples.english: To clean one's ears with a cotton swab.

examples.japanese: {薬局|やっきょく}で{綿棒|めんぼう}を{買|か}ってきて。
examples.english: Go buy some cotton swabs at the pharmacy.

examples.japanese: {細|こま}かい{部分|ぶぶん}の{汚|よご}れは{綿棒|めんぼう}を{使|つか}うときれいに{落|お}とせる。
examples.english: You can cleanly remove dirt from small areas by using a cotton swab.

notes:
A common household item. Composed of {綿|めん} (cotton) + {棒|ぼう} (stick/rod). An everyday word that every learner living in Japan will encounter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {綿棒|めんぼう}で{耳掃除|みみそうじ}: ear cleaning with a cotton swab
- {綿棒|めんぼう}で{塗|ぬ}る: to apply (medicine/cosmetics) with a cotton swab
- {使|つか}い{捨|す}ての{綿棒|めんぼう}: disposable cotton swabs
- {先|さき}の{細|ほそ}い{綿棒|めんぼう}: cotton swabs with thin tips

USAGE:
While commonly used for ear cleaning in Japan, medical professionals often advise against inserting cotton swabs into the ear canal. {綿棒|めんぼう} is also used for applying medicine to wounds, cleaning small electronics, and precision cosmetics application.

RELATED TERMS:
- {耳掃除|みみそうじ}: ear cleaning
- {耳|みみ}かき: ear pick — a traditional Japanese ear-cleaning tool, different from a cotton swab
- {脱脂綿|だっしめん}: absorbent cotton; cotton wool — the medical cotton used for gauze and padding
